card.name: Right after a drug name, before its verb
card.fires_on: The small word or punctuation right after a drug name or drug class that is the subject of a warning sentence, just before the verb. Examples are a comma, "tablets", "capsules", "may", or "in" after "differ".

modes.label: Comma after drug name
modes.description: A comma follows a named drug or class that is the subject, before a phrase like "have been reported" or "can cause".

modes.label: Dosage form after drug name
modes.description: The dosage-form word (tablets, capsules) follows the full drug name just before the main verb.
modes.example: Dimethyl fumarate delayed-release<< capsules>> may decrease lymphocyte counts.

modes.label: Word linking drug to its effect
modes.description: A linking word such as "in" or "may" follows a drug subject, ahead of the effect being described.
modes.example: Whether antipsychotic drug products differ<< in>> their potential to cause tardive dysk

card.writes: It slightly favors "enter" and "entered" forms, which is a weak and unclear output effect.
card.plain: It fires at the point in a warning sentence where the drug has just been named and the statement about what it does is about to start.
